resources.string: The head unit rejected source authentication after TLS completed. It may require an identity from an issuer it trusts. Trusting the head unit or regenerating a self-signed identity does not establish that trust.

Select a PEM file containing your source certificate, any intermediate certificates in issuer order, and matching unencrypted RSA-2048 private key. Use an identity you are authorized to use. A valid import replaces the current source identity; head-unit pins stay in place. Importing does not guarantee that the vehicle will accept it.

TLS profile (tls12-cbc-compat only after a recorded ClientHello shows the need)
Trust the next wired head unit for this attempt (C2 first use; its certificate is pinned if TLS completes)
Capture raw discovery response for diagnosis (discovery only; the exported report then contains unredacted head-unit name, serials, vehicle id, and Bluetooth address — handle it as sensitive)
Video configuration (largest by default; a head unit can advertise one it will not display while still acknowledging every frame, so pin a size to compare)
Encoder frame rate (negotiated by default; a lower rate also lowers the H.264 level and bitrate, which tells a decoder limit apart from a resolution limit)
Keep bodies of messages we do not interpret (diagnostic; bytes are unexamined)
Save the encoded video stream for offline decoding (diagnostic; tens of MB)
Open every advertised channel, as Android Auto does (diagnostic)
Resume the encoder instead of rebuilding it when focus returns (diagnostic)
Wireless only: ping the car over its Wi-Fi every 50 ms, so the phone\'s Wi-Fi does not doze while the screen is off. Cleared, it pings once a second, only to measure the delay
When the head unit keeps falling behind the video, restart the stream as switching screens does
Wait for unsolicited video focus instead of asking, as Android Auto does
Keyframe interval (Android Auto configures 60 s; this source used 1 s)
AV setup request field 1 (codec-type is the vendored schema; config-index is aasdk\'s reading, for a head unit that decodes the wrong configuration)
Scene area (content letterboxes into the advertised content rectangle; frame draws across the whole frame, treating the margins as a safe area the head unit overlays)

Vehicle sensors to subscribe to during projection (all by default, which reads every type the head unit advertises to record which of them carry real values; restriction is driving status and night data; none subscribes to nothing)

Also record the vehicle\'s latitude and longitude in the report. Position identifies the vehicle, so it stays out of reports unless you turn this on; without it the report still says whether the head unit sent a position, never where.

Turn-by-turn on the vehicle\'s own cluster: send the next maneuver of the route being followed to the instrument display behind the wheel. Needs no permission; the cluster shows nothing until a destination is set, and the head unit may show nothing at all, which affects nothing else.
Play the fixed demonstration sequence on the cluster instead of the route — for checking the cluster without a destination or a drive.

Send the maneuvers even if the vehicle never offers its cluster: some head units advertise the service and then stay silent, and this turns one drive into two answers — whether it offers the cluster, and what it shows when told regardless. The report records that nothing was waited for.

Audio out over USB: send this app\'s own audio (a test tone) to the vehicle speakers. Needs no permission — the audio is generated here, not captured from another app — and the head unit may refuse it, which affects nothing else.
Media controls: let the head unit\'s transport buttons control whatever is playing on this phone, and tell it what is playing

Transport buttons (play/pause, next, previous) work now and need no permission. To also show the track on the head unit, and to make rewind and forward move exactly %1$s, Android requires notification access — there is no narrower permission for reading another app\'s media session. Granting it lets this app see every notification on the phone. It reads them only for features you turn on: with Notifications on the dashboard on, it reads alerting notifications to show them in the car, and with Call controls on it may read call notifications to answer or end a call. It keeps them in memory for the drive only and never saves or reports them. With those off, it reads none. You can withdraw access in Settings at any time, and media controls keep working.
Notification access granted: the head unit is told what is playing.
Notification access not granted: transport buttons work; the head unit is told nothing is playing.
Keepalive (mirror follows the head unit\'s ping encryption, initially encrypted after TLS; plaintext or encrypted overrides it)

A named place the dashboard lists for one-tap routing. Keep the name short: it is drawn large enough to read from the driver\'s seat. The location takes the same forms as the destination box — lat,lon, a geo: URI, or an OsmAnd link. Names and coordinates stay on this phone and out of every report.
Name, as shown on the head unit

Pick or create a folder, such as Download/OpenAuto. Any .map or .rd5 file put there is checked and moved into this app when this screen opens, so it is never stored twice. A file that fails its check stays in the folder. All installed maps are drawn together and routing uses every installed tile, so a trip across regions needs nothing switched.

That is the OsmAnd maps folder. Choose a different folder to drop files in.
Start projecting when plugged in (only a head unit already trusted)
12- or 24-hour times on the dashboard (clock, arrival, weather) and in the route line here. Takes effect when projection next starts.
No destination. Share a place from OsmAnd, type one below, or tap a favorite.
The dashboard\'s first tile lists them, and a tap on one routes there. Names and coordinates stay on this phone and out of every report.
Tap to route there. Drag ≡ to reorder. Touch and hold to rename, move to the top or remove.
Everything a drive needs is in place.
Automatic follows the head unit\'s day and night signal. Day or Night keeps the dashboard in that palette. The ☀/☾ button on the dashboard changes the same choice.
Send even if the cluster stays silent

Shows alerting notifications in the dashboard\'s second tile: the app, the sender or title, and one line of text. Needs notification access. They are held in memory for the drive only, and never saved or reported. Turned off, no notification is read.
No app has posted a notification yet this session. With notifications on the dashboard, apps appear here once they post one, and can then be hidden.

Answer, decline and hang up calls from the dashboard. Turned off, the app never sees a call. With a one-time grant from a computer, mute and a keypad work too; without it, the phone\'s own call notification is used, which needs notification access. Callers, numbers and keypad digits are never saved or reported.

A notification tapped on the dashboard is read aloud: the sender and the text, never the app. The full text is fetched from the phone at the moment of the tap and handed to the speech engine; it is not saved, logged or reported. Speech plays only while the phone is connected to Bluetooth audio, and is heard in the truck only while Bluetooth audio is its selected source. Tap the row again to stop it.

What playing media does while the phone speaks, for read-aloud notifications and turn prompts alike. Pause media asks the player to pause for a moment; well-behaved players resume by themselves afterwards, and one that ignores it keeps playing under the voice. Lower volume has Android turn the player down while the phone speaks; podcast and audiobook players often pause instead.
Speech: %1$s (this engine can use the network)
Looking for other routes… A long trip can take a minute.

resources.string: No other route that is not mostly the same roads.
Could not look for other routes: %1$s
No map is installed, so the routes are drawn on a plain background.
The route changed while the preview was open (a re-route or a new destination), so the choice was not applied.
Avoided roads cost more rather than being closed, so a place only reachable that way is still reached. A change recomputes the route being shown, from where you are now.

Roads mapped as motorways, and their ramps, are made much more costly, so a route leaves them for almost any other way: Austin to Temple left I 35 and took 117 minutes instead of 65. That is the interstates and most freeways; a highway with junctions and traffic lights is not a motorway and is not avoided.
Roads tagged as toll roads, and toll booths, are all but closed. Around Austin this keeps a route off SH 130. A toll road missing its tag on OpenStreetMap is not avoided.

Roads mapped as gravel, dirt or other unpaved surfaces, and rough tracks, are timed as even slower than they already are, so a route takes them only where there is no paved way. Unpaved roads are already avoided where there is a good paved way; this makes the avoiding stronger. A road with no surface on the map is taken to be paved.
Prefers roads outside cities and large towns, even when going through is quicker. Routes can get much longer: Austin to Temple went from 109 to 132 km.
Also routes over farm and forest tracks and roads of unknown class, which are closed to routes otherwise. For ranch roads and the like; leave off for ordinary driving.

The fastest the route\'s times assume you drive, where the road allows it. A road with a lower speed limit on the map is still timed at its limit, and bends, junctions and traffic lights slow it further. This also decides how much a highway is preferred, so a higher speed can change the route, not only its time.\n\n56 mph is the routing engine\'s own value; it timed every interstate mile at 56 mph and put Austin to Dallas at 3 h 42 min. 75 mph put it at 2 h 56 min.

Adds to or takes from every time the route estimates: the time to the destination, the arrival time, and the time to each turn. Use it if arrivals are always early or late by about the same share. It changes no route.
Show other routes on the map

While a route is followed on the truck\'s screen, the phone looks for up to two other ways to the destination about every five minutes and draws them in grey, each with how much longer it is (\"+6 min\"). Tap a bubble on the truck\'s screen to take that route. One goes away once you pass the point where it leaves your route. Routes more than ten minutes longer (or a quarter of the time left) are not shown. Looking takes the phone some seconds of work each time, and never holds up a re-route.

As you drive, the time still to go is corrected by how your drive so far compared with its estimate: slow traffic makes the arrival later, a clear road earlier. It starts after about two minutes of driving, counts in full after ten, never takes off more than a third or adds more than half, and starts afresh for each new destination. It is not used for the time to the next turn.

Turn prompts are spoken while a route is followed. This is the same switch as the speaker button beside End route on the dashboard: turning either one changes both, and it stays as it was left for the next drive. Prompts are spoken only over Bluetooth audio, and are heard in the truck only while Bluetooth audio is its selected source.

Up to three prompts for each turn. Early comes about 50 seconds ahead, and never less than half a mile, and only on long stretches. Prepare comes about 15 seconds ahead. At the turn comes a few seconds before it. The faster you drive, the further ahead each one comes. Untick any you do not want to hear.
Earlier gives every prompt about a third more time ahead of the turn, and Later about a quarter less. The shortest distances ahead stay the same.
Brief says the distance and the turn. Full also says the next turn when two come close together (\"then turn left\"), and \"keep right\" before a motorway exit that follows a keep.

\"Turn right onto Main Street\" rather than \"Turn right\". Route numbers are said in words, so I 35 is \"Interstate 35\" and FM 1826 is \"Farm to Market 1826\". The dashboard and the cluster are not changed.
Says \"Rerouting\" once when you leave the route and a new one is worked out.
Says \"You have arrived\" once at the destination.

Says \"In 500 feet, turn right onto Main Street\" the way a turn prompt is said: over Bluetooth audio only, with media paused or lowered as While speaking is set, and not during a call. It is played even with turn prompts switched off, so you can check the truck hears the phone before a drive. With no projection running, the speech engine is started for the sample and stopped after it.
Spoken over Bluetooth audio. If the truck was silent, check that Bluetooth audio is its selected source.
Spoken (lab Bluetooth override: no Bluetooth device was checked).
Not spoken: no text-to-speech engine is installed, or it failed to start. Choose one in Text-to-speech settings on Home.
Not spoken: the speech engine has no English voice. Add one in Text-to-speech settings on Home.

Shows the Diagnostics tab, with every protocol option, the source identity and pins, and the reports, and adds the debug line to the dashboard\'s header.
Keep Wi-Fi awake during wireless projection
Restart video when the car falls behind

The next head unit this phone connects to is trusted for this one attempt, and its certificate is pinned if the secure connection completes, so later drives can start on their own. Only do this plugged into a vehicle you use.

The map and routes follow the vehicle\'s own position when the head unit sends one, and need nothing from the phone for it. With location allowed, the phone\'s position is used when the vehicle has none, and a destination can be routed before you plug in. The position stays on this phone and is never put in a report.
The current weather in the dashboard\'s header, read from Breezy Weather on this phone. No network.

Shows the current weather in the dashboard\'s header; tap it there for the next few hours. An active weather alert takes the second tile over notifications. It is read from Breezy Weather\'s data on this phone, with a permission Breezy asks you for when this is turned on, and nothing connects to the network. The reading is held in memory for the drive only; no place, temperature or alert is saved or reported. Off, nothing is read.
An alert at or above the level below is read aloud once, the first time it appears in a drive: \"Weather alert\" and its headline. Speech plays only over Bluetooth audio, like turn prompts.
Heard only while the dashboard\'s voice toggle is on.
The lowest severity of alert that takes the dashboard\'s second tile and is spoken. Alerts below it still show in the weather view opened from the header.
Address search and map places, read from OsmAnd\'s own map files on this phone. Nothing is copied or written, and nothing connects to the network.

Choose the folder OsmAnd keeps its maps in. This app gets permission to read it, never to change it, and reads only the .obf map files directly inside it. The drop folder is a separate choice and is kept.
In OsmAnd: Settings → OsmAnd settings → Data storage folder → Manually specified. Your maps are in Documents/osmand.

That is the drop folder. Choose the folder OsmAnd keeps its maps in.
The most Gas, Food or Shop markers drawn at once on the map, nearest the centre first, so a busy downtown does not bury the map.
While a route is followed, a Gas, Food or Shop button searches this far along the route ahead, or to the destination if that is nearer.
How far either side of the route a place may be and still count as along it.
How many of the nearest places ahead get their detour worked out. More finds a better stop and takes longer.
No OsmAnd maps to search. Choose their folder in Settings → OsmAnd maps.
